gloss: one by one; one at a time

definitions.gloss: one by one; one at a time; one each
definitions.explanation: Indicates doing or distributing something one unit at a time. The counter 個 is used for small, discrete objects.

examples.japanese: お{菓子|かし}を{一個|いっこ}ずつ{配|くば}る。
examples.english: To hand out sweets one each.

examples.japanese: {卵|たまご}を{一個|いっこ}ずつ{割|わ}って{入|い}れてください。
examples.english: Please crack and add the eggs one at a time.

examples.japanese: {問題|もんだい}を{一個|いっこ}ずつ{片付|かたづ}けていけば、いつか{全部|ぜんぶ}{終|お}わる。
examples.english: If you tackle the problems one by one, you'll eventually finish them all.

notes:
{一個|いっこ}ずつ means 'one at a time' or 'one each,' using the versatile counter {個|こ} for small, discrete objects.

COMMON PATTERNS:
Part of the ～ずつ pattern, which attaches to a quantity to mean 'each' or 'at a time.' The same structure works with other counters:
- {一人|ひとり}ずつ (one person at a time)
- {一枚|いちまい}ずつ (one sheet at a time)
- {一本|いっぽん}ずつ (one [long object] at a time)
- {少|すこ}しずつ (little by little)

USAGE:
- Very common in everyday speech because {個|こ} is a general-purpose counter for small objects
- Often used for distributing items: お{菓子|かし}を{一個|いっこ}ずつ{配|くば}る (hand out sweets one each)
- Also used for doing things methodically: {問題|もんだい}を{一個|いっこ}ずつ{解|と}く (solve problems one at a time)
